question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

lobbying.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards (H RES 1498)
plain_language: This resolution censures Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A Yea votes to censure him. A Nay votes not to.

lobbying.bill_title: In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards.

question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. This vote would have delayed that bill until the Commerce Secretary published a report on how trade fights with Canada and China, and the war in Iran, affect fishing costs and seafood prices. A Yea would have added that delay; a Nay rejected it.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran
